The deadline watcher had a rough stretch. From early Wednesday morning until just after midnight Thursday, it failed to log in to Canvas forty-five times in a row. Deadlines weren't being watched during that time. Once it recovered, it found your physics lab prelab on Impulse and Momentum, nearly eighteen hours overdue. It completed and submitted it on its own. Every answer was correct, but the late penalty left you with four out of five.

On grades, the physics lab also posted a four and a half out of five on the Simple Harmonic Motion prelab, and it sits at an A. Abstract Algebra posted a score of three on the chapter one homework. The one score to watch is Linear Algebra, at sixty-seven and a half percent, a D plus. Prokaryotic Cell is at an A minus, and Physics is a B plus.

In your email, Physics put out a note that the professor was away at a conference, and a learning assistant named Neerav covered office hours near room twenty-one eighty. That's past now, but it's worth knowing if you need help with homework nine.

Your language department wrote about the FLATS exam. They assumed you didn't want to take the one scheduled for Thursday. When you're ready, you'll need to register again with the proctoring service. A few dates are coming up. Emerging Scholars applications are due Sunday, and Florida Undergraduate Research Conference abstracts are due Monday. On Monday from ten to two, the financial aid office hosts a FAFSA help event in the Reitz Union.

Spring registration opened Friday at two in the afternoon. The automatic plan was set to try adding six classes the moment it opened. This data can't confirm whether that worked, so check your schedule.

The most important thing today is Physics homework nine, due tonight, if it isn't already in.

Projects

You have six things today. The most time-sensitive is for calculators, also called kalq. You answered that the Meta Business Manager and ad account should be set up now, so the account builds history before any conversion ads. There's no conversion spend yet. Also for kalq, the launch configuration for PreProduct needs your browser admin access, for the PreProduct and Notifications screens. And the privacy policy still needs a publish date from you.

For AlphaThread, you still need to create the free Alpaca market-data key file in your secrets folder. Two research tasks are waiting on it, and it's unclear whether the file exists yet.

For the Discord feed, the daily health step failed again. The listener is running and connected, but it reports two hundred sixteen unfilled gaps, so deletes inside those gaps are invisible. Yesterday it was one gap.

Two deadlines. The device interface pack promised to Wonderful PCB is due Saturday, November seventh. And you need to verify the seven Globex holiday and early-close times against CME's final tables before November twenty-sixth.

Now the projects. AlphaThread development had a productive night. The overnight queue finished five items. The robustness battery is now wired into the backtest record. The plan for the first two stories of the robustness spec is done, along with its review leftovers. The trend and regime overlay for the premium-selling strategies is finished, and the third story, a robustness gate criterion, landed too. Separately, the Vest one-step presets and sleeve-budget rules are committed. That's thirteen commits in a day, mostly on the robustness branch. The main checkout sits on the signal sleeve branch, clean. The decisions you were asked about yesterday no longer show up as open, so work moved past them. Still blocked are the opening-range breakout study and the SPY momentum study, both on the Alpaca key. The Vest presets still need a route to copy a real backtest database before a first real run. On the earlier spec, five tasks stay open, and one of them must land before any promotion. The runner is healthy, with no alerts.

For calculators, the overnight run ended fine with six tasks done. It applied your founder answers to the security page and the product page, finished a working first-hour checklist, added official EU legal sources, followed up on the European security standard, and added a security-updates question to the product FAQ. Your answers are recorded, and the order-confirmation draft is now ready to start. A reply went to Wonderful PCB with your choices, and the device pack is queued. Fourteen commits sit on the overnight branch, not pushed. The overnight guard denied two shell commands that touched its own guardrails. The run report says nothing was lost. At launch, you'll need a security thank-you page and an acknowledgments entry in the security file.

The Discord feed did its curation. The watch list is down to one hundred six channels across twelve servers, thirty-four fewer than yesterday, including several alert channels. Gold Squad, Odd Lots, TPE's School and Quanted still have nothing worth watching. The config file has uncommitted changes. Next step is finding out why health failed and whether those gaps can be filled.

IG ideas is fine. The watcher ran at six this morning, analysed fourteen new posts, and produced no new ideas. Seven posts are still waiting on transcripts, five from velocity options and two from rp dot profits.

The other three AlphaThread checkouts are idle, with nothing new. One has two uncommitted price cache files.

That's the picture. The Meta account and the Alpaca key are the quickest wins today.

Markets

Friday was a sharp, tech-led selloff. The Nasdaq 100 fell about three and a half percent, and money moved into energy, health care and staples.

The S&P 500 dropped about one point eight percent. The Dow lost about one percent. Small caps fell about one point six percent. The big indexes traded at roughly twice normal volume, which shows real conviction. Sellers were committed, not just drifting. Small caps traded on normal volume, so that drop is less convincing.

Tech did the damage. The sector fell nearly five percent on more than double normal volume. Energy rose almost two percent and closed at a one-year high. Staples gained about one and a half percent, also at a high. Gold fell about three percent to a one-year low, roughly thirty percent below its peak. Oil rose about two percent to around one hundred and four dollars. The ten-year yield slipped to about four point nine percent.

Now the unusual parts. First, the single-stock wreckage. Intel fell nearly thirty percent on about four and a half times normal volume, after opening about twenty-six percent lower. Reddit fell about the same, on nearly seven times normal volume. A gap down that holds all day on that much volume usually means big institutions were selling, not just retail traders.

Second, rotation. Forty-five S&P stocks hit one-year highs, many in energy, health care and staples, against five at lows. When money flees one corner and piles into defensive ones, it can mean investors are repositioning, not abandoning stocks altogether.

Third, breadth. Decliners beat advancers, two hundred seventy-five to two hundred twenty-eight. That is a fairly mild split for an index down nearly two percent. The share of stocks above their fifty-day average actually edged up, to about sixty-one percent. One read is that the pain was concentrated in a few huge tech names, not broad. One day is not a trend.

The VIX rose about two points to roughly nineteen. Its three-month cousin sits a bit higher, which is still the calm arrangement. The put to call ratio rose to about point six six.

Why? Investing.com says Wall Street closed sharply lower as fears over AI cash burn sparked a tech selloff. MarketWatch reports Intel had its worst day in decades, a one hundred forty billion dollar wipeout. CNBC reports S&P revised its outlook on Meta downward over cash flow and capital spending concerns. MarketWatch also says Reddit logged its biggest one-day drop ever. Why gold fell is less clear, though MarketWatch notes it dropped to its lowest in a year despite renewed Iran jitters.

Concept of the day: the VIX versus the three-month VIX. Normally near-term fear is lower than fear about the next three months, so the ratio sits below one. Yesterday it was about point eight nine. Today it rose to about point nine four. Still below one, but closer. If the VIX ever rises above the three-month reading, traders are paying more to protect against the next few weeks than the next few months. That usually signals acute stress. Today the market moved in that direction, without getting there.

AlphaThread

Yesterday was a busy day for your put spread sleeve. It opened three new trades and closed three, all on underlying stops. Those stops pushed its total realized profit down fifteen dollars, to about eight dollars. One of the new trades is still open. That sleeve is now at eight of twenty trades toward going live. Paper profit uses mid-price fills, so treat it as an upper bound.

On health, nothing halted and no reconciliation breaks. Your three running sleeves had no restarts in the last day. Your flow levels futures sleeve no longer shows a version, because no build manifest was found for it. It was version zero point one yesterday.

On research, three studies changed status. The question of whether Instagram creators' stock calls predict anything is still active, and the one creator tested so far does not predict direction. The low relative volatility study and the follow-up on whether implied vol underprices what comes next both say they need a better test. No new ideas came into the inbox.

For R eleven, the score did not move. You have two closed real trades, averaging plus zero point three two R. Four placebo trades average plus one point nine three. The bar needs thirty closed real trades, a mean of at least plus zero point one five, and a lead over the placebo. So it is far from either.

Now the roll call.

Nothing is live yet. Your broker is Interactive Brokers, but the account is only approved for the simplest options level.

On paper, your put spread sleeve is running in the main store. It has eight closed trades and is up about eight dollars. It is at thirteen of ninety days.

Your copy Mordy sleeve is running cleanly with no trades yet. It is at zero of twenty trades and five of ninety days.

Your flow levels sleeve is running cleanly with two closed trades, up eleven dollars. It is at two of twenty trades and four of ninety days.

Your flow levels futures sleeve is running with no trades yet. It is at zero of twenty trades and one of ninety days. Its latest research session allows uncovered short legs, so it cannot go live as it stands.

On research, R eleven is collecting data. R ten, on copying a Discord caller, needs more data, with nine calls against forty required. R twelve, on insider cluster buys, is pre-registered and waiting on your approval of a contact string for the SEC. R four is waiting on your approval of one probe to close it out. R three is waiting on your review. R five, on expanding the capture universe, needs a better test.

Six other studies are closed or answered. The inbox holds sixty-two ideas, and twenty-nine are queued.

The most important thing today is spring registration at two, so make sure your plan is ready, and then get started on that physics homework.

Projects

Here is what needs you today.

Discord feed first. The health check failed again this morning, and the listener still has one unfilled gap. Deletes inside that gap are invisible, so it's worth investigating.

AlphaThread has the most decisions. First, whether to put a free Alpaca data key in your secrets folder. That unblocks two research studies. Second, whether to buy minute history for NQ futures. The recommendation is no. Third, whether a failed robustness battery should block a promotion from research to paper. The recommendation is no, just record it. Fourth, how a real backtest reaches the survival command, and which strategy and rule set it should use. There is also a deadline. Before November twenty-sixth, check the seven Globex holiday and early-close times for 2026 against the final CME tables.

Four research tasks are built but blocked on your decisions. Spec twenty-four, the robustness record, is drafted and clarified. Next is planning its first two user stories, and the third waits on your promotion answer. Five items on spec twenty-three are still open. The project stays marked blocked, as it was yesterday.

Calculators, kalq. The overnight run finished three queued tasks and added the belief-brief fields. The FCC re-check could start today, and part of it is done, using the FCC order and the Sunshine notice. The rest waits for the adopted FCC order, and is pencilled in from November sixth. Your founder answers from today are recorded. The overnight branch has eighteen commits and has not been pushed. Next are small document cleanups in the security, product data, and comment filter files. Still blocked are one task needing a publish date, and one needing your browser admin access.

IG ideas ran fine. The watcher found thirteen new ideas from three hundred and four posts, a big jump from none yesterday. The inbox now holds sixty-two ideas, with twenty-nine queued. The six visible new ideas all scored three and can be executed live, but none is queued. Eleven posts are waiting for transcripts, six from one creator and five from another.

Discord feed. Curation added seven channels, so you now watch one hundred and forty channels across twelve servers. Four servers were judged not worth watching, same as yesterday. The listener is connected with about forty-four hundred events logged. The health failure is the one thing to chase, and it's the second day running.

Kalq-discord. You approved five outreach messages and a track of directory targets, capped at one hundred. Three messages went out, one directory was pitched through a moderator channel, two were skipped, and one is on hold. The rest wait on the blocks mentioned earlier.

That's the picture. The Discord health check is the quickest thing to look at, and the AlphaThread decisions are the most valuable.

Markets

Wall Street had a lopsided Thursday session: a handful of giant tech and software names fell hard, while most of the market quietly went up.

The S&P 500 slipped about point four percent on roughly normal volume. The Nasdaq 100 fell about one point four percent, also on normal volume. The Dow lost about point four percent. Small caps went the other way, up about one percent, though on lighter volume than usual, so that move is easier to reverse.

The sector picture shows the split. Health care rose about two point four percent on nearly one and three-quarters times normal volume, and closed at a one-year high. Heavy volume on a high shows real buying. Real estate, staples and utilities each rose about one and a half percent or more. Communication services fell about one point nine percent on over one and a half times normal volume, and closed at a one-year low. Tech fell about one point two percent.

Now the unusual part. Google's two share classes each dropped about twelve percent on more than five times normal volume. ServiceNow fell about twenty-seven percent on six times normal volume, and Fortinet fell about twenty percent. All of these gapped down at the open. A gap on volume like that usually means new information arrived overnight, often earnings, and big holders repriced all at once instead of selling gradually. The headlines here don't say what triggered it, so the cause is unclear.

Second, breadth. About four hundred and six stocks in the S&P 500 rose, against ninety-seven that fell. The share above their fifty-day average improved to about sixty-six percent, from about sixty-one percent five days ago. So the index decline came from a few large stocks, not broad weakness.

Third, fear gauges stayed calm. The VIX sat at about seventeen, below the three-month VIX at about nineteen. That is the normal shape, and it suggests no near-term panic. The equity put to call ratio was about point five eight, which means traders were leaning toward calls.

Elsewhere, the ten-year yield eased about one percent to just under five percent. Bitcoin fell about four percent on nearly one and three-quarters times normal volume. CNBC reports Binance suffered a hack of about six point three billion dollars, which plausibly explains the selling. Oil settled around one hundred and two dollars, and energy edged up. CNBC reports Exxon and Chevron beat earnings expectations on strong refining profits.

Looking ahead, CNBC reports Amazon was down about seven percent and Intel down about twenty-five percent in premarket trading after earnings, and Investing.com says European shares dipped on AI cash-burn fears. That is a possible follow-through for tech, but it's one morning.

Concept of the day: the S&P 500 is weighted by company size, so a few huge stocks can pull the index down even when most members rise. Yesterday showed it clearly. About four hundred stocks advanced, yet the index fell, because Alphabet and other heavyweights dropped sharply. When the index and breadth disagree, ask whether the move is concentrated in a few names or genuinely broad. Here it was concentrated, which is often less worrying than a decline led by many stocks.

New script format (cold open, signposting, closing recap) in af_heart with natural sentence and paragraph pauses, an intro sting, chimes between segments and an outro. No background music, no think pauses; a decision marker becomes a short silence.

Script

Today: four things need you, and the biggest is the AlphaThread paper run that is supposed to start counting today.

First, AlphaThread. You need to start the five-session paper run today. It needs five consecutive trading sessions beginning this Monday, with at least one open and close. After that comes a repeat with a position open, and then the final validation. The Schwab token was assumed to lapse on Sunday, and it is unclear whether you renewed it.

Second, still AlphaThread. You need to check that the runner is really active. The process has been up for about forty-three hours. But the newest log, written sixteen hours ago, says only that the runner finished. The data does not say whether that is normal.

Third, kalq. You need to answer the privacy follow-ups. They cover which ad pixel events and hashed email go to ad partners, and pixels on by default in the US but only after accept in the EU and UK. They also cover the thirteen-plus and under-sixteen position, the split between eighteen-plus in the Terms of Sale and thirteen-plus for accounts, and export through the account page only.

[[think]]

Fourth, also kalq, three smaller asks. Answer the firmware questions: whether over the air updates are a launch requirement, the signing key, the api address, and the photo limit. Tell the briefing what came out of Sunday's Shenzhen meeting, since the outcome isn't recorded. Then give the alert email address and sender, and say whether to push to the dev theme and turn on the customer privacy setting.

[[think]]

Now, what changed.

AlphaThread is flagged for attention. On Sunday afternoon, three commits landed on main. The OptionsDX importer is merged, and that roadmap item is marked done. No tasks changed. Seventy-one are done, and two remain open, both of which only you can close. Next is the five-session run, then the validation run and recording the counts. After the merge, the next spec will be number twenty, the pricing ladder. Health shows a warning, the runner oddity you just heard about. No alerts went out in the last day, and there were no collection errors.

kalq is blocked. The overnight run finished six tasks. The privacy policy now reflects the four new decisions. The backend has the thirteen-plus check, consent purge, and an alert stub. Data retention purges are in, along with a test for parallel sessions against account deletion, and a closer for stuck credit reservations that records spend before making the call. Footer privacy links are built in local theme files, not pushed. Sunday also brought the four decisions, a supplier log update, and research on four G and SIM feasibility. Tests pass: one hundred twenty-nine for functions and one hundred fifty-two for the database.

Still unverified: real Supabase behaviour, the scheduled jobs, and the theme links in a browser. Next up is a run-through on the Supabase dev project and a spend-reserve test with concurrency. The firmware work waits on your answers, and the privacy page still needs a publish date. The FCC vote is October twenty-ninth, and that re-check can't start before October thirtieth. Nothing to do on that today.

If you remember one thing, start the AlphaThread paper run today, after confirming the runner is really active.
